proposition: On Suʾl al-Mulūk, New Brethren says it was written for Shāhrukh in early 1426, at the instance of his son Bāysunghur, as an attempt to cultivate Shāhrukh's patronage after Iskandar's fall. The dissertation says it was written at Bāysunghur's request and for Bāysunghur, before 7 Rajab 829/15 May 1426 (asterisked), one day before Nafsat al-Maṣdūr I, and it places Shāhrukh's first favour at c. 1422. Both agree that it ends with a prognostication from Shāhrukh's name of a century of Timurid glory.
